SENT VIA CERTIFIED MAIL / WRITTEN DISPUTE SUBMISSION
DATE: October 26, 2026

TO:
St. Luke's Ambulatory Surgical Pavilion
Attn: Patient Financial Services & Billing Dispute Department
450 Medical Center Way, Boston, MA 02115
Phone: 1-888-555-7890

RE: FORMAL NOTICE OF BILLING ERROR, DISPUTE OF OVERCHARGES, AND DEMAND FOR ACCOUNT RECONCILIATION
Patient Name: Michael Chang
Account / Invoice Number: SURG-2026-4410
Statement Date: 2026-10-18
Total Disputed Amount: $1943.00

Dear Billing Compliance Officer,

Please accept this letter as formal written notice of billing errors, improper coding discrepancies, and excessive charges regarding the above-referenced account. I am exercising my rights under the Fair Credit Billing Act (15 U.S.C. § 1666), Regulation Z (12 C.F.R. § 1026.13), and federal hospital billing standards.

A comprehensive forensic audit of the itemized statement reveals that the gross billed total of $2360.00 contains $1943.00 in computational inaccuracies, unbundled procedures, duplicate entries, and markups that substantially exceed regional Medicare benchmarks.

============================================================
ITEMIZED SCHEDULE OF DISPUTED CHARGES
============================================================
1. CPT 80053 — COMPREHENSIVE METABOLIC PANEL
   • Date of Service: 2026-10-15
   • Billed Amount: $340.00 | Benchmark Median: $52.00
   • Violation: Excessive Markup (6.5x Medicare Benchmark)
   • Disputed Overcharge: $262.00
   • Forensic Remedy: Demand recalculation to the regional fair market standard of $78.00, saving $262.00.

2. CPT 82040 — ALBUMIN SERUM
   • Date of Service: 2026-10-15
   • Billed Amount: $120.00 | Benchmark Median: $18.00
   • Violation: Improper Unbundling (CCI Violation)
   • Disputed Overcharge: $120.00
   • Forensic Remedy: Component test must be written off to $0.00 in compliance with CMS National Correct Coding Initiative.

3. CPT 82040 — ALBUMIN SERUM
   • Date of Service: 2026-10-15
   • Billed Amount: $120.00 | Benchmark Median: $18.00
   • Violation: Excessive Markup (6.7x Medicare Benchmark)
   • Disputed Overcharge: $93.00
   • Forensic Remedy: Demand recalculation to the regional fair market standard of $27.00, saving $93.00.

4. CPT 84075 — ALKALINE PHOSPHATASE
   • Date of Service: 2026-10-15
   • Billed Amount: $130.00 | Benchmark Median: $20.00
   • Violation: Improper Unbundling (CCI Violation)
   • Disputed Overcharge: $130.00
   • Forensic Remedy: Component test must be written off to $0.00 in compliance with CMS National Correct Coding Initiative.

5. CPT 84075 — ALKALINE PHOSPHATASE
   • Date of Service: 2026-10-15
   • Billed Amount: $130.00 | Benchmark Median: $20.00
   • Violation: Excessive Markup (6.5x Medicare Benchmark)
   • Disputed Overcharge: $100.00
   • Forensic Remedy: Demand recalculation to the regional fair market standard of $30.00, saving $100.00.

6. CPT 71046 — CHEST X-RAY 2 VIEWS
   • Date of Service: 2026-10-15
   • Billed Amount: $490.00 | Benchmark Median: $68.00
   • Violation: Excessive Markup (7.2x Medicare Benchmark)
   • Disputed Overcharge: $388.00
   • Forensic Remedy: Demand recalculation to the regional fair market standard of $102.00, saving $388.00.

7. CPT 93000 — 12-LEAD ELECTROCARDIOGRAM COMPLETE
   • Date of Service: 2026-10-15
   • Billed Amount: $310.00 | Benchmark Median: $42.00
   • Violation: Excessive Markup (7.4x Medicare Benchmark)
   • Disputed Overcharge: $247.00
   • Forensic Remedy: Demand recalculation to the regional fair market standard of $63.00, saving $247.00.

8. CPT 96360 — INTRAVENOUS HYDRATION INFUSION 1ST HOUR
   • Date of Service: 2026-10-15
   • Billed Amount: $550.00 | Benchmark Median: $88.00
   • Violation: Excessive Markup (6.3x Medicare Benchmark)
   • Disputed Overcharge: $418.00
   • Forensic Remedy: Demand recalculation to the regional fair market standard of $132.00, saving $418.00.

9. CPT J7030 — NORMAL SALINE 1000ML
   • Date of Service: 2026-10-15
   • Billed Amount: $420.00 | Benchmark Median: $14.00
   • Violation: Excessive Markup (15.0x Medicare Benchmark)
   • Disputed Overcharge: $378.00
   • Forensic Remedy: Demand recalculation to the regional fair market standard of $42.00, saving $378.00.


============================================================
STATUTORY DEMANDS & PRESERVATION OF RIGHTS
============================================================
1. IMMEDIATE STAY ON CREDIT REPORTING & COLLECTIONS:
Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. § 1666(a) and 12 C.F.R. § 1026.13, you are strictly prohibited from reporting this disputed account as delinquent to any consumer credit reporting agency or assessing late finance charges while this formal dispute is pending. Any collection activity must cease immediately.

2. TIMELY WRITTEN ACKNOWLEDGEMENT:
Federal law requires written acknowledgement of this notice within thirty (30) days of receipt, and a complete resolution or written explanation within two billing cycles (not to exceed 90 days).

3. COMPREHENSIVE ITEMIZED LEDGER DEMAND:
I formally demand an updated, itemized statement containing standard CMS Revenue Codes, 11-digit National Drug Codes (NDCs) for all administered pharmaceuticals, and verified physician charge summaries.

4. CHARITY CARE & AMOUNTS GENERALLY BILLED (AGB) DISCLOSURE:
In accordance with Internal Revenue Code Section 501(r)(4) and (r)(6), provide a complete copy of your Financial Assistance Policy (FAP) application and recalculate all remaining legitimate charges to your hospital's Amounts Generally Billed percentage.

Until these disputed charges are investigated and adjusted in accordance with federal and state billing regulations, no payment on the disputed sum of $1943.00 will be remitted.

Sincerely,

____________________________________
Michael Chang
Account Holder / Patient Representative
Certified Mail Tracking: _______________________
statutoryCitations: Fair Credit Billing Act (15 U.S.C. 1666) — Timely notice of computational billing error and automatic credit report stay.
CMS National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) — Prohibition against improper component unbundling.
Internal Revenue Code Section 501(r)(6) — Tax-exempt hospital Limitation on Charges to Amounts Generally Billed (AGB).
Federal No Surprises Act (Public Law 116-260) — Protection against non-consensual out-of-network balance billing.
phoneNegotiationPoints: Script 1 (Account Verification): "Hello, I am calling regarding Account #SURG-2026-4410. I have submitted a formal Fair Credit Billing Act dispute regarding $1943.00 in duplicate and unbundled line items. Please confirm this account is tagged as 'In Active Dispute' so no automated collections trigger."

Script 2 (When representative says 'Rates are non-negotiable'): "I understand hospital chargemaster rates are standard, but federal IRC Section 501(r) prohibits non-profit hospitals from billing patients more than the Amount Generally Billed (AGB). Several line items on this bill exceed Medicare median allowables by over 400%. What is your facility's current AGB percentage for this year?"

Script 3 (Handling Unbundled CPT Codes): "Line item CPT 82040 is a component of comprehensive panel 80053 billed on the same date. Under CMS NCCI guidelines, component testing cannot be billed separately. Please write off this unbundled charge."

Script 4 (Lump-Sum Settlement Offer): "If you recalculate the statement to fair market Medicare median rates of $417.00, I am prepared to settle the entire undisputed balance today with a single one-time payment in exchange for a written zero-balance release."
